result.answer:
Verdict: SUPPORTED

The paper reports that memory CD4+ T cell responses enhance production of multiple innate inflammatory cytokines and chemokines (IICs) in the lung and that, during influenza infection, this leads to early control of virus [S:0fa1cd0cafa7#2]. It further states that memory CD4+ T cell–induced IICs and viral control require cognate antigen recognition and are optimal when memory cells are TH1 or TH17 polarized, but are independent of IFN-γ and TNF-α and do not require activation of conserved pathogen recognition pathways [S:0fa1cd0cafa7#3]. The authors describe this as a mechanism by which memory CD4+ T cells induce an early innate response that enhances immune protection against pathogens [S:0fa1cd0cafa7#3].

Limitation: only the released abstract is available [S:0fa1cd0cafa7#2], so the specific chemokines and the direct causal evidence that chemokines (rather than other IICs) mediate viral control are not shown.
